speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you describe when the swelling and pain in your right ring finger started and if there was any specific injury or trigger?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text: Did you hear or feel a "pop" at the time of injury, and are you currently able to fully straighten the tip of your finger?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive swelling and pain in the right ring finger. I also have Inability to flex the right ring finger at the distal interphalangeal joint when making a fist, Pain at the distal interphalangeal joint, Extended right ring finger in resting position.

speaker: Doctor
text: You are describing a classic "Jersey Finger" injury, which is a rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon. Let me examine the finger to confirm the diagnosis and check for any associated fractures.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant medical history. Social history: Student and active in sports, particularly football. Non-smoker and drinks alcohol socially.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: No bone fractures or dislocations visible. Soft tissue swelling noted around the distal interphalangeal joint of the right ring finger.

speaker: Doctor
text: The X-ray rules out a fracture, which strongly supports the diagnosis of a flexor digitorum profundus tendon avulsion. To confirm the extent of the tendon injury and plan for surgery, I need to visualize the soft tissues. REQUEST TEST: Hand_Ultrasound

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal ultrasound is unexpected given the clinical signs, so I will request MRI imaging to definitively visualize the tendon rupture. REQUEST IMAGES

speaker: Patient
text: Denies fever, numbness, or tingling in the affected finger.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the mechanism of injury and clinical presentation, I am confident in the diagnosis despite the normal ultrasound. DIAGNOSIS READY: Jersey Finger (Flexor Digitorum Profundus Avulsion)

DIAGNOSIS_READY_Answer: Rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon at its point of insertion
